harmonicFunction: Em (i) - Rebellious, energetic tonic minor chord driving the furious Australian punk tempo
C (bVI) - Submediant chord providing anthemic emotional lift in the chorus climb
G (bIII) - Relative major chord providing melodic optimism and crowd-chant resonance
D (bVII) - Subtonic chord maintaining unstoppable forward momentum
B7 (V7) - Dominant seventh chord with major leading tone (D#) injecting classic 1950s rockabilly snap

techniques.name: Rockabilly Hybrid Picking & Double Stops
techniques.description: Holding a flatpick between thumb and index finger to strike bass notes while using the middle and ring fingers to snap simultaneous double stops on higher strings at 168 BPM

notes: Grip pick firmly with thumb and index; curl middle and ring fingers underneath strings 2 and 1
Snap middle and ring fingers upward with percussive attack to produce the signature Gretsch twang
Mute bass strings with the fleshy heel of the palm while keeping upper strings ringing crisply
Maintain strict syncopated sixteenth-note subdivision at high tempo
sequence: Downstroke low open E root with pick
Pluck double stop at frets 12 and 12 on strings 2 and 1 with middle and ring fingers
Slide down chromatically to frets 10 and 10
Execute rapid hammer-on/pull-off on the G string
tips: Chris Cheney plays a Gretsch 6118 Anniversary hollowbody guitar with TV Jones Classic Filter'Tron pickups
Use a short slapback tape delay (120ms with single repeat) to reproduce authentic rockabilly echo
Start practicing hybrid picking slowly at 100 BPM to build independent finger strength

techniques.name: Rapid Tremolo Picking & Chromatic Runs
techniques.description: High-speed continuous alternate picking on single strings at 168 BPM combined with chromatic fret-hand walking lines up and down the neck

notes: Keep pick strokes minuscule and close to the string surface
Rotate wrist from the forearm without tensing shoulder or bicep muscles
Coordinate chromatic finger steps (1-2-3-4) in exact sync with pick oscillations
Use the neck pickup or bridge Filter'Tron for crisp, percussive cut
sequence: Begin tremolo picking on high E string at fret 12
Execute full whole-step bend on fret 15 with screaming vibrato
Rapid descending blues scale run resolving to low E root
tips: Use a heavy, stiff pick (1.0mm or heavier) to prevent pick drag during high-speed tremolo
Rest the palm lightly near the bridge for stability, but don't mute the high E string
Count triplets and sixteenth notes steadily to prevent rushing ahead of the beat

sections.name: Intro Slap-Bass Pulse & Monster Rockabilly Riff
sections.description: Scott Owen's upright bass slaps out the frantic intro before Chris Cheney's Gretsch explodes into iconic rockabilly hybrid-picked double stops at 168 BPM.
notes: Pick-and-finger hybrid attack on the high double stops
Sharp staccato snapping on upbeat sixteenths
B7 dominant turnaround sets up the punk-rock explosion
Lock seamlessly into the blistering 168 BPM pocket

sections.name: Verse 1 High-Speed Punk Chug
sections.description: 'Well we don't need no one to tell us what to be!' - rapid downstroke palm-muted power chords driving beneath Cheney's defiant Australian vocals.
notes: Tight palm muting on the downbeats
Rapid shifts across 6th and 5th string power chord roots
Accented syncopated pushes on beat 4-and
Maintain relaxed wrist motion to avoid forearm fatigue

sections.name: Chorus Aussie Punk Anthem
sections.description: 'Cause I'm a prisoner of society! Another casualty of society!' - full unmuted punk chords ring out with explosive gang-vocal energy.
sections.progression: Em - C - G - D - Em - C - G - B7
notes: Full-power chord assault across all measures
Hit the B7 chord hard on the turnaround to inject rockabilly tension
Keep the tempo steady without rushing the 168 BPM pace
High-energy release into the next verse

sections.name: Rockabilly Guitar Solo Masterclass
sections.description: One of the greatest guitar solos in Australian rock history: Chris Cheney unleashes a masterclass of high-speed rockabilly licks, tremolo picking, double-stop bends, and chromatic cascades.
sections.progression: Em - A7 - Em - B7 - C7 - B7
notes: High-speed alternate tremolo picking on the high E string
Double-stop bends on frets 12 and 14 across G and B strings
Chromatic descending walk down from fret 15 to fret 12
Finish with blazing rockabilly triplet flourish into the final chorus
sections.exerciseLabel: Chris Cheney Blistering Rockabilly Solo Study

sections.name: Bridge Breakdown & Bass Slap Solo
sections.description: Scott Owen takes a show-stopping upright slap-bass solo while Cheney provides clean, syncopated Gretsch rhythm accents and ambient feedback.
notes: Sparse staccato chord punches on the upbeats
Subtle Bigsby vibrato arm dips create spooky rockabilly pitch waver
Dynamic build from quiet ticking to thunderous roar
Explosive drum fill into the final chorus

sections.name: Outro Climax & Tremolo Finale
sections.description: Furious final chorus repetition culminating in Cheney's screaming high tremolo picking and a thunderous unison stop.
notes: Maximum punk assault and rapid pick speed
Climb high onto the neck with frenetic tremolo picking
Tight unison stop on the final low Em chord
Bigsby vibrato arm shake into feedback

beginner.title: Power Chords & High-Speed Punk Rhythm
steps: Learn Em, C, G, and D power chord shapes
Practice downstroke palm muting at 120 BPM before accelerating to 168 BPM
Master the transition from verse muting to chorus strumming

intermediate.title: Rockabilly Hybrid Picking & B7 Turnarounds
steps: Learn the pick-and-finger hybrid picking technique on the intro double stops
Practice the B7 dominant turnaround with clean fret-hand placement
Build pick-hand stamina to sustain high-tempo sixteenth notes

advanced.title: The Masterclass Solo & Full Song Performance
steps: Transcribe and perform Chris Cheney's blazing rockabilly guitar solo
Master high-speed tremolo picking without pick drag or tension
Perform the complete 3:52 track with unyielding punk energy

commonMistakes: Using all flatpick on the intro riff instead of hybrid picking, losing the percussive snap on the upper strings
Tensing the pick-hand forearm during the fast 168 BPM verse downstrokes, leading to muscle fatigue
Sloppy muting on the high double stops, causing open strings to buzz
Rushing the tempo during the guitar solo instead of locking into Scott Owen's slap-bass groove
practiceRoutine: 10 mins: Hybrid picking warm-up drills combining pick downstrokes with middle finger snaps
10 mins: Slow metronome practice of the intro riff at 110, 135, and 168 BPM
10 mins: Tremolo picking alternate stroke exercises on single strings
10 mins: Full speed solo transcription study focusing on clean note transitions
focusAreas: Pick-and-finger hybrid picking independence and tone balance
Pick-hand wrist economy during high-speed 168 BPM punk downstrokes
Clean execution of rockabilly chromatic runs and double-stop bends
metronomeWork: Start the intro double-stop riff at 110 BPM with a metronome to ensure timing accuracy
Increase tempo in 5 BPM increments once 4 consecutive flawless cycles are played
Set click to beats 2 and 4 to develop authentic rockabilly swing and pocket
